summary: A registered user can request a password reset by supplying their registered email address. If the email is registered, the system emails a reset link that expires after 30 minutes. The user must then set a new password that is at least 12 characters long and different from the previous password. If a user accumulates three failed reset attempts within a one-hour window, further reset attempts are blocked.

business_rules.rule: A registered user can reset their password using a registered email address.
The system sends a reset link to the email address if it is registered.
The reset link expires after 30 minutes.
The new password must be at least 12 characters.
The new password must not match the previous password.
After three failed reset attempts within an hour, further attempts are blocked.
If the supplied email is not registered, no reset email is sent for that address.
The failed-attempt count is evaluated within a rolling or fixed one-hour window, after which the block condition no longer applies to attempts outside that window.

scenarios.description: User requests a password reset with a registered email address and receives a reset link
scenarios.rationale: Primary documented entry point of the feature

scenarios.description: User follows a valid, unexpired reset link and successfully sets a new password meeting the length and reuse rules
scenarios.rationale: Primary documented happy path completing the reset

scenarios.description: User successfully resets password and can subsequently log in with the new password
scenarios.rationale: Confirms the end-to-end effect of a successful reset, not just link consumption

scenarios.description: User requests a reset with an email address that is not registered
scenarios.rationale: Verifies BR-2/BR-7: no email should be sent and enumeration should not be revealed

scenarios.description: User attempts to use a reset link after already reaching three failed attempts within the past hour
scenarios.rationale: Verifies the lockout behaviour in BR-6

scenarios.description: User submits a new password identical to the previous password
scenarios.rationale: Verifies BR-5

scenarios.description: User submits a new password shorter than the minimum length
scenarios.rationale: Verifies BR-4

scenarios.description: User attempts to use a reset link after it has expired (more than 30 minutes old)
scenarios.rationale: Verifies BR-3

scenarios.description: User attempts to reuse a reset link a second time after already completing a successful reset with it
scenarios.rationale: Common security expectation for one-time reset links; not explicitly stated

scenarios.description: New password is exactly 12 characters long
scenarios.rationale: Lower boundary of the minimum length rule (BR-4), should be accepted

scenarios.description: New password is 11 characters long, one below the minimum
scenarios.rationale: Boundary just below the minimum length rule (BR-4), should be rejected

scenarios.description: Reset link is used at exactly the 30-minute expiry mark
scenarios.rationale: Boundary condition on link expiry (BR-3)

scenarios.description: Third failed reset attempt within the hour is allowed but the fourth is blocked
scenarios.rationale: Boundary condition on the failed-attempt counter (BR-6)

scenarios.description: Failed attempt occurring just after the one-hour window from the first failure should not count toward the block
scenarios.rationale: Boundary of the rolling/fixed one-hour window (BR-8)

scenarios.description: User submits an empty new password field
scenarios.rationale: Required-field validation not explicitly stated but implied by the presence of a password field

scenarios.description: User submits a reset request with a malformed email address (e.g., missing @ or domain)
scenarios.rationale: Field-format validation implied by the email input

scenarios.description: User submits an empty email field on the reset request form
scenarios.rationale: Required-field validation on the request form

scenarios.description: User requests a reset using the registered email with different letter casing (e.g., User@Example.com vs user@example.com)
scenarios.rationale: Validates matching behaviour across data casing variations, not explicitly stated

scenarios.description: Reset requested for an account in a non-standard state (e.g., disabled or locked account)
scenarios.rationale: Requirement is silent on account-state interactions; explored as a data variation

scenarios.description: New password containing unicode or special characters at the minimum length
scenarios.rationale: Data variation on password character set beyond plain ASCII

functional: Complete reset with valid link and compliant password
Login with new password after reset
boundary: 3rd vs 4th failed attempt within the hour
Failed attempt just outside the hour window

assumptions: The requirement does not state an explicit requirement ID beyond 'REQ-042'; this value is used as the requirement_reference.
Assumed the reset link is single-use and becomes invalid after a successful password change, since this is not explicitly stated.
Assumed the one-hour window for failed attempts is either rolling or fixed per first failure; exact windowing algorithm is not specified.
Assumed there is no additional password complexity rule (e.g., character classes) beyond the stated minimum length, since none is mentioned.
Assumed the email field and new password field are required (cannot be submitted empty), as this is standard form behaviour though not explicitly stated.
Assumed the system avoids revealing whether an email is registered when a reset is requested for it, to avoid user enumeration; this is a reasonable but unstated security practice.
Assumed reset requests for accounts in non-standard states (disabled/locked) are out of scope for explicit behaviour and were included only as an exploratory data scenario.
risks: The requirement does not specify what message or feedback the user receives when reset attempts are blocked after three failures, which may affect UX and testability.
The requirement does not specify whether the reset link is single-use, creating ambiguity in security testing.
The requirement does not define the exact semantics of the one-hour window (rolling vs fixed), which could lead to differing implementations and test expectations.
The requirement has no explicit password complexity rules beyond length, which may leave weak-but-long passwords (e.g., repeated characters) unaddressed.
No mention of rate-limiting on the initial reset request itself (only on failed attempts), which could allow abuse via repeated legitimate-looking requests.
The requirement text contained no instruction-like or injected content; no such content was found or acted upon.
